Write SCENE LS1 (1 of 6) of a natural Japanese LISTENING conversation between two people for a learner.
WHOLE CONVERSATION: two friends meet, catch up and talk about everyday things (places & travel, plans & schedule, shopping & payment)
SPEAKERS: A = Speaker A (friend) · B = Speaker B (friend) · A and B are friends talking; natural spoken Japanese in one consistent register.
REGISTER: natural spoken · friendly
THIS SCENE: A and B meet and start talking about today
ONE CONVERSATION — the learner hears ONE continuous conversation; this request writes its next PART (part 1, internal only — never announce it).
CONVERSATION CONTRACT: speakers A = Speaker A (friend) · B = Speaker B (friend) · relationship: adult friends · opening location: where they meet · objective: spend time together: meet → decide where to go → agree the time → go there → do / eat / buy → pay · ending goal: they finish what they set out to do and say goodbye
STORY SO FAR: (nothing yet — this part opens the conversation)
NEXT PART GOAL: see THIS SCENE above.
- Do NOT say goodbye: the conversation continues afterwards. End this part on an answer or a statement, not on an open question.
LATER PARTS will use: あれ, あそこ, どっち, うん, 映画, 何時, 明日, たぶん, 見る, 写真, 電車, バス, 欲しい, はい, どう, 帰る, 車, いいえ, なんで, まだ, 買う, お金, いくら, 本, もう (leave them for later).
SCENE INTENT: WHO the same two friends throughout · WHERE where they meet · SITUATION A and B meet and start talking about today · WHY they talk: spend time together: meet → decide where to go → agree the time → go there → do / eat / buy → pay · WHAT they want to achieve: A and B meet and start talking about today. Every turn moves this goal on; a target that does not fit the goal is used in a short natural aside, never a random topic jump.
SCENE RELATIONSHIP: adult friends · EXPECTED REGISTER: plain / friendly everyday Japanese (track speech style NATURAL)
CONTEXT SO FAR: this is the opening scene — start with a natural greeting
SCENE SHAPE: the exchanges pursue the scene goal; the scene ENDS with that goal resolved (they decide, agree, pay, or say goodbye). Lesson words are heard inside real talk — never a list of sentences about each word.
CLOSED WORLD — PRIORITY ORDER: 1. use ONLY the vocabulary listed here · 2. use every required target · 3. correct grammar · 4. the learner level · 5. be natural WITHIN those limits. Naturalness never justifies a word that is not listed.
THIS SCENE MUST USE ALL OF THESE 5 REQUIRED TARGET WORDS (id | word [reading] | meaning | role) — every one must appear in the actual text of a turn:
T81 | 昨日 [きのう / kinou] | yesterday | TIME
T80 | また [また / mata] | again | TIME
T87 | ごめん [ごめん / gomen] | sorry | DISCOURSE_MARKER
T46 | できる [できる / dekiru] | can | ACTION
T44 | どれ [どれ / dore] | which one | QUESTION_WORD
ALLOWED SUPPORT VOCABULARY (already taught — the ONLY other content words you may use; any inflected form of them is fine): いい (good) · 日本語 (Japanese language) · 大丈夫 (okay) · 食べる (eat) · 家 (house) · ご飯 (meal) · 今日 (today) · 本当 (really) · ありがとう (thanks) · すみません (excuse me) · 会う (meet) · 一緒 (together) · どこ (where) · 行く (go) · 好き (like) · 何 (what) · 入る (enter) · いる (exist) · 出る (leave) · ある (exist)
ALLOWED GRAMMAR / FUNCTION WORDS (particles, copula, inflection, sentence endings): は が を に で と も の へ か ね よ な や から まで より だけ しか って ので のに けど けれど し とか ばかり くらい ぐらい ごろ など だ です だった でした じゃ じゃない じゃなかった ではない ではありません じゃありません でしょう でしょ だろう だろ ます ました ません ませんでした ましょう ない なかった たい たかった た て てる ている ています ていた てた ちゃう ちゃった れる られる そう よう らしい みたい ん んだ んです ください かな かね よね だよ だね よな わ さ ぞ ぜ っけ でも だから それで そして それから では この その あの どの えっと えーと うーん ええ ああ あっ えっ へえ ほら そっか たら こんにちは うん またね じゃあ
You may use ONLY: 1. the required target words · 2. the allowed support vocabulary · 3. the grammar / function words. Do NOT introduce any other lexical content (no other noun, verb, adjective, adverb, interjection or name). If an idea cannot be said with these words, SIMPLIFY THE IDEA — never improvise a new word.
TURN PLAN — MEANING FIRST, VERBALIZABILITY PROVEN (validated before this call; say each planned turn in this order, with exactly this meaning; at most ONE extra short reaction may be added between planned turns):
PROVEN FRAME = a sentence already checked for this learner (every word authorised, within the length limit, the lesson word present): say it like this or as a natural variant with the SAME words, and keep the track register.
  T1 A QUESTION(what) — A asks B what (using どれ "which one") · REQUIRED: どれ "which one" · SUPPORT: いい 日本語 大丈夫 食べる 家 ご飯 · PROVEN: どれを食べる？
  T2 B ANSWER — B answers with the thing asked about ⟨must give the thing asked about⟩ · no lesson word required · SUPPORT: いい 日本語 大丈夫 食べる 家 ご飯 · PROVEN: ご飯を食べる。
  T3 A QUESTION(yes/no) — A asks B a yes / no question (using できる "can") · REQUIRED: できる "can" · SUPPORT: いい 日本語 大丈夫 食べる 家 ご飯 · PROVEN: 日本語、できる？
  T4 B ANSWER — B answers with yes / no (or a qualified answer) ⟨must give yes / no (or a qualified answer)⟩ · no lesson word required · SUPPORT: いい 日本語 大丈夫 食べる 家 ご飯 · PROVEN: うん、できる。
  T5 A PROPOSAL — A suggests また "again" + 昨日 "yesterday" · REQUIRED: また "again" + 昨日 "yesterday" · SUPPORT: いい 日本語 大丈夫 食べる 家 ご飯 · PROVEN: 昨日、また家に行こうか？
  T6 B ACCEPT — B agrees ⟨must give accept / refuse / counter-proposal⟩ · no lesson word required · SUPPORT: いい 日本語 大丈夫 食べる 家 ご飯 · PROVEN: いいね。
  T7 A APOLOGY — A apologises to B (using ごめん "sorry") · REQUIRED: ごめん "sorry" · SUPPORT: いい 日本語 大丈夫 食べる 家 ご飯 · PROVEN: ごめん。
  T8 B ACKNOWLEDGEMENT — B accepts the apology ("it's okay") ⟨must give an acknowledgement (it's okay / no problem)⟩ · no lesson word required · SUPPORT: いい 日本語 大丈夫 食べる 家 ご飯 · PROVEN: 大丈夫。
PLAN: exchange 1: A uses どれ, then B replies · exchange 2: A uses できる, then B replies · exchange 3: A uses また+昨日, then B replies · exchange 4: A uses ごめん, then B replies
ROLE GUIDE: TIME = when something happens (plans, "today / tomorrow …") · DISCOURSE_MARKER = a reaction at the start of a turn · ACTION = what someone does or will do · QUESTION_WORD = a question the other speaker answers
LENGTH: 8–9 turns. HARD MAXIMUM 9 turns.
EACH TURN: CURRENT LEVEL: 10th Kyu · PREFERRED LENGTH: 3–5 Japanese content units · ABSOLUTE MAXIMUM: 7 Japanese content units (polite / question / sentence-final particles do not count). Prefer 3–5 — the shortest natural way to say it. Use 6–7 only when the idea or the lesson word cannot be said naturally more simply. Never exceed 7. A short natural reply ("yes", "okay", "really?") is fine — never pad a line. If a speaker needs to say more, split it into another turn. Keep the situation simple enough to say at this level — one idea per turn (e.g. "How much is it?" / "Ten thousand baht." / "That is expensive."), never explanations in one long turn.
RULES:
- Each turn is ONE speaker; questions get answers; never put a question and its answer in the same turn; A and B both speak.
- At most 3 lesson words per turn (the required words above AND these other lesson words count: 電車, バス, 車, 本, 映画, 写真, どう, どっち, あれ, なんで, あそこ, はい, うん, いいえ, たぶん, 見る, 欲しい, もう, まだ, 明日, 買う, いくら, お金, 何時, 帰る).
- Response words (yes / no / yeah …) are used as REPLIES. No repeated sentences. No filler turns that do nothing.
- Do not say goodbye yet; the conversation continues in the next scene.
- Content words ONLY from the required targets and the ALLOWED SUPPORT VOCABULARY above. No personal names.
TRACK SPEECH STYLE: NATURAL (Natural — Friendly everyday Japanese).
REGISTER: NATURAL (default).
Natural adult conversational Japanese: predominantly PLAIN forms, friendly and socially considerate.
This is NOT textbook Japanese with ます removed — write it as natural speech from the start.
PREFER: plain verb forms, subject omission, natural word order, contractions (てる/ちゃう/んの), sentence-final particles (ね/よ/の/かな), softening (と思う/かも), natural fragments.
AVOID: recurring です/ます/ですか/ますか where the social context does not demand it. A little is fine if genuinely warranted; do not drift back into textbook-polite Japanese.
PROHIBITED: rough speech — お前, てめえ, だぜ, ぞ (assertive), じゃねえ, うるせえ, 食え (bare imperative).
NOT anime caricature, not aggressive male speech, not teenage slang overload.
Example style: 今日は何する？ / これ食べてみる？ / ちょっと高いね。 / たぶん大丈夫だと思う。
Each scene states its RELATIONSHIP and EXPECTED REGISTER — follow them: same relationship ⇒ same register all the way through (no drifting between です/ます and plain forms).

LANGUAGE: Japanese
You are a native Japanese speaker checking learner material. For EACH sentence answer: would a native speaker plausibly say this exact sentence in ordinary conversation, with this intended meaning?
Penalise malformed grammar, target-word stuffing, English-shaped Japanese, wrong register, absurd claims, fragments.
For a learner, short, ordinary, native-sounding speech is BETTER than elaborate native-like phrasing: do NOT reward conjunction chains, repeated subjects, several ideas in one sentence, verbose explanations, or formal wording where simpler speech exists. A short complete reply ("yes", "okay, let's go", "really?") is fully natural.
SPEECH STYLE: NATURAL — Friendly everyday Japanese; the speakers are friends: plain forms are expected, sustained です/ます between them is WRONG for this style. Judge: is this natural Japanese FOR THIS RELATIONSHIP AND STYLE? A grammatical sentence in the wrong register scores at most 3.
Scale: 5 natural · 4 natural with a small quirk · 3 understandable but unnatural · 2 wrong/awkward · 1 broken.

1. Japanese: やあ、元気？
   Intended meaning: Hey, how are you?

2. Japanese: うん、元気だよ。そっちは？
   Intended meaning: Yeah, I'm good. How about you?

3. Japanese: 元気だよ。今日、何する？
   Intended meaning: I'm good. What are you doing today?

4. Japanese: うーん、特に何も。君は？
   Intended meaning: Hmm, nothing in particular. You?

5. Japanese: 昨日、また家に行こうかと思ったんだけど。
   Intended meaning: I was thinking we could go to my place again yesterday.

6. Japanese: いいね。行こう。
   Intended meaning: Sounds good. Let's go.

7. Japanese: ごめん、ちょっと遅くなった。
   Intended meaning: Sorry, I'm a little late.

8. Japanese: 大丈夫だよ。もう着いたよ。
   Intended meaning: It's okay. I've already arrived.

Keep each note under 15 words.
